Thirty-seven percent to eighty-six. One switch.
And you've probably got this switch at work.
A big American company changed one thing in its retirement plan, in April 1998.
Before, new staff had to sign themselves up.
After, they were signed up automatically, unless they said no.
Same pay. Same plan. Same match.
In their first year or so, thirty-seven percent of the old group had joined.
But most never touched the setting again. Three percent, parked in the safest fund.
The default decided for them. So check what your switch says.
